summary: The note describes the Texian Army, a military force of volunteer and regular soldiers that fought the Mexican army during the Texas Revolution. About 3,700 men joined between the Battle of Gonzales on October 2, 1835, and the end of the war at the Battle of San Jacinto on April 21, 1836. After independence it became the Army of the Republic of Texas, which merged with the US Army in 1846 after Texas was annexed by the United States, with Sam Houston becoming commander in chief of the new Texas army.
one_line: The Texian Army was the volunteer and regular force that fought Mexico in the Texas Revolution, later becoming the Republic of Texas army.
key_facts: The Texian Army was also known as the Army of Texas and the Army of the People.
The Texian Army was a military organization of volunteer and regular soldiers who fought against the Mexican army during the Texas Revolution.
Approximately 3,700 men joined the Texian Army between October 2, 1835, and the end of the war.
Recruitment into the Texian Army began during the Battle of Gonzales on October 2, 1835.
The Texas Revolution ended on April 21, 1836, at the Battle of San Jacinto.
After gaining independence, the Texian Army was officially known as the Army of the Republic of Texas.
In 1846, after the annexation of Texas by the United States, the Army of the Republic of Texas merged with the US Army.
Sam Houston became the new commander in chief of the new Texas army after the 1846 merger.
